title: Profit cash and equity
goal: Distinguish earning revenue, receiving cash, incurring an expense, and distributing profit.

slides.title: Can a profitable business run short of cash?
slides.takeaway: Revenue and cash can arrive at different times.
slides.notes: This is one transaction, not the full company profit.

slides.title: Revenue is recognized when earned

rows: Receive advance for next month’s service

slides.takeaway: For these simple services, completion establishes earning.
slides.notes: This is an introductory simplification, not the full model for complex contracts.

slides.title: Expenses are recognized when incurred

items.heading: June utilities used
items.text: An unpaid $200 invoice creates Utilities Expense and Accounts Payable.

items.heading: Future insurance paid
items.text: A $600 payment for July coverage creates Prepaid Insurance.

slides.takeaway: A payment is not automatically this period’s expense.
slides.notes: The utilities invoice is an ordinary source transaction, not a required period-end adjusting entry.

slides.title: A credit sale and its collection are separate events
slides.takeaway: Do not record the collection as revenue again.

slides.title: Cash received early can create a liability
slides.lead: Receive $900 for services to be performed in July.
slides.takeaway: The business owes a service, so it has a liability.
slides.notes: The service is still unperformed at June 30. Do not invent an extra June entry.

slides.title: Contributions and dividends are separate from profit
slides.takeaway: Contributions and distributions are separate from profit.
slides.notes: The borrowing row is a separate cash example, not the case’s vendor-financed van. Firms raise funds for operations and investment as well as shortages.

slides.title: The retained earnings balance connects past and current results

blocks.text: Ending retained earnings = Beginning retained earnings + Net income − Dividends
Retained earnings is accumulated profit after distributions, not a separate reserve of cash.

slides.takeaway: Do not add profit again after using ending retained earnings.
slides.notes: A net loss reduces retained earnings; a negative balance is an accumulated deficit.

slides.title: Operating, investing, and financing explain business activity

items.heading: Operating
items.text: Provide services, sell inventory, and pay operating costs.

items.heading: Investing
items.text: Acquire or sell long-term productive assets.

items.heading: Financing
items.text: Raise capital or borrow; pay dividends or repay principal.

slides.takeaway: Week 11 applies these categories to cash movements.
slides.notes: Inventory payments are operating; not every asset purchase is investing.

slides.title: Try it: identify the effects on profit and cash
slides.notes: Separate practice set. Ask for the other account on each cash movement.
